newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industry chief wants more export tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industry chief wants more export tax cuts.

text.p: A recent move exempting Brazilian exports from a so-called ICMS tax is not enough to reduce the country's trade deficit and the government should offer exporters more tax cuts, a leading industrialist said.

"We have to cut more taxes on exports to export more," Antonio Emirio de Moraes, vice-president of industrial conglomerate Grupo Votorantim said after meeting with Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
In September, Brazil eliminated the Tax on the Circulation of Merchandise and Services (ICMS) for exports and on the importing of capital goods in a bid to give the economy a shot in the arm.
Exports paid ICMS of up to 13 percent, although several categories of goods were already exempt.
Moraes said exporters should also be exempted from two types of employee contributions, known by their Portuguese acronyms COFINS and PIS. Votorantim is a major producer of cement and pulp and paper.
